outcome: No proof, disproof, or partial resolution of the core conjecture (does every convex polyhedron have a non-overlapping edge unfolding) was found in the window; the only in-window work found is on a related, opposite-direction question about constructing overlapping unfoldings.
summary: Shephard's problem / Dürer's conjecture — whether every convex polyhedron has a non-overlapping edge unfolding (net) — remains open as of September 2026, with no proof, disproof, or partial case resolved in the 26 Jan 2024–present window. The strongest positive result on record, Ghomi's theorem that every convex polyhedron admits a net after an affine transformation, dates to 2013–2014 (arXiv:1305.3231, published in Geometry & Topology 2014) and is well outside the window. The most recent negative/adjacent result, Barvinok and Ghomi's pseudo-edge-graph counterexample (a polyhedron unfoldable along no pseudo-edge graph), is from 2019, also predating the window, and in any case concerns pseudo-edges (geodesic cuts not restricted to actual polyhedron edges) rather than the standard edge-unfolding the conjecture is about — a related problem, not a case of this one. The one paper found dated inside the window, 'Overlapping Unfoldings of Cones and Convex Polyhedra' (arXiv:2607.09606, submitted 10 July 2026), proves the opposite-direction fact that convex polyhedra exist whose edge- or non-edge unfoldings overlap by any prescribed thickness. This does not bear on whether every convex polyhedron has *some* non-overlapping net — it is a different question about how bad worst-case overlaps of specific constructions can be — so per §3.1 it is a related problem/variant, not a scope-narrowing case, and does not move the status. No AI system is mentioned in that paper or in any other source consulted; all work found uses classical geometric/combinatorial construction and proof techniques. A widely covered 2026 OpenAI announcement of an AI model disproving 'a central conjecture in discrete geometry' was checked and confirmed (via secondary sources, since openai.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher) to concern the Erdős unit-distance problem, an unrelated conjecture — not Dürer's conjecture or Shephard's problem — so it is not recorded here. The Wikipedia 'Net (polyhedron)' article's own account of the state of the art stops at 2019, consistent with no intervening progress. Overall this is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' case matching the triage's 'none' verdict, which is confirmed rather than disagreed with.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2026 overlapping-unfoldings paper is at least adjacent 'progress' worth a `progress` status, since it sharpens understanding of how unfoldings can fail to be simple. But per §3.1's test — does it change what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry, which asks specifically about existence of a non-overlapping edge unfolding — it does not: it neither narrows the conjecture's territory nor bears on whether a net exists for any given polyhedron, so `open`/`no_change_found` is the correct call rather than `progress`.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving or disproving, for the standard edge-unfolding definition, that every convex polyhedron has a non-overlapping net (or exhibiting/ruling out a counterexample under ordinary edge cuts, not pseudo-edges), or a case-restricting result (e.g., resolving it for a broad new class of polyhedra beyond the affine-transformed or thin/flat cases already known).
